src/retry.rs.what: Calls the bank again when a call fails for a reason that passes: at most six tries, each wait longer than the last and at a random point.
src/retry.rs.change: It used to wait half a second, three tries at most. Now each wait may double, to 30 seconds, at a random point, six tries at most.

parts.says: Runs `call`, and after a failure that may pass, waits and tries again; a failure a retry can’t fix comes back at once, as [[Transient errors]] do.
parts.before: Waited a fixed half second between tries.

parts.says: The longest the next wait may be: 200 milliseconds, doubled for each try so far, never past 30 seconds. That is [[Exponential backoff]].
**Waits a random time below that ceiling, so callers that failed together don’t all come back at once.** That is [[Jitter]].
The first wait is about 200 milliseconds, no wait is longer than 30 seconds, and a call is tried at most six times.

out.says: A half-second pause between every try, with three tries at most. The growing, random wait replaces it.

src/bank/breaker.rs.what: A circuit breaker for the bank: after five failures in a row it stops calls for a while, then lets one through to see if the bank is back.
src/bank/breaker.rs.change: New: calls to a bank that’s down used to go out anyway, and wait to fail.

parts.goal: Lets a call through, or not
parts.says: Closed, every call goes. Open, a call is turned away at once with how long to wait. Once it has cooled off, one call goes to test the bank: [[Circuit breakers]].
A call that worked closes the breaker. Five failures in a row open it; a failed test opens it again. A declined card doesn’t count.
A test call that failed for its own reasons, such as a declined card, says nothing about the bank, so the next call tests it instead.
A timeout, a bank that can’t be reached, or an error on its side counts; anything else is the bank working as it should.
Closed counts failures in a row; open turns calls away until a time; half open lets one call through. The breaker keeps the state, and how many failures and how long a wait. [[State]]
From the settings, or from numbers given straight, as the tests do. It starts closed.

parts.goal: Takes a token for a call
parts.says: Fills the bucket for the time since it was last filled, then takes a token, or says how long until there’s one: [[Rate limiting]].
Sleeps until a token is due, then takes it, so calls that wait together are let through one at a time: [[Thundering herd problem]].
Adds the tokens earned since it was last filled, never more than the burst.
A burst of three goes at once, the fourth waits 100 milliseconds, and an hour idle still allows only three.

parts.goal: A bucket, and how it fills

parts.says: **The key is claimed with an insert before anything is charged, and the stored row comes back in the same statement.** A new key goes ahead; a key answered before gets its answer; one still going is told so: [[Idempotency keys]].
Keeps the status and body a request was answered with, under its key, so the next copy gets the same.
Frees a key whose request failed before anything was charged, so the caller can send it again and have it go ahead.
A claim left five minutes with no answer, because ledger stopped, is taken over by one copy of the request: the one that moves its time.
A hash of the request’s body, so the same key sent with a different request is turned away, not answered: [[Hash function]].
Deletes answers older than a day; no shop retries a request that late.
